q: Where in SPP Document 202 is the Group VI (Repetitive Construction, Except Housing) fee schedule found?
n: The Group VI repetitive-construction schedule is Sec. 6.3.6 of the SPP Document 202 building-group fee provisions, immediately following the Group V (Monumental) schedule. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: If the client had built a fifth Mausoleum on the same unamended plans, how much additional fee would that fifth building add to the P5,280,000.00 total for the first four?
n: The fifth building falls under "4th and succeeding buildings," so it is also charged 30% of the base RPF: 0.30 x P2,400,000.00 = P720,000.00, the same amount as the fourth building. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)
scenario: Scenario: An architect's original design for a Mausoleum was implemented four (4) times on four different sites. The same set of plans/design and related Contract Documents was re-used for all four buildings without any amendment to the drawings or specifications. The Mausoleum falls under Group V (Monumental), with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P20,000,000 for each building, and the client engaged the architect for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS), billed at 12% of PCC.

q: What is the Professional Fee for the fourth (4th) Mausoleum building?
n: The fourth building is charged 30% of the base RPF: 0.30 x P2,400,000.00 = P720,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)
scenario: Scenario: An architect's original design for a Mausoleum was implemented four (4) times on four different sites. q: Before any repetition discount, what group and base rate governs the Recommended Professional Fee for the Mausoleum design used in this scenario?
o: Group V (Monumental), DAEDS at 12% of PCC
Group VI, at a flat rate set only by the number of buildings
Group III, DAEDS at 7% of PCC
n: Mausoleums are listed under Group V (Monumental buildings and other facilities requiring consummate design skill and much precise detailing), with a DAEDS rate of 12% of PCC. That Group V rate is the "RPF for type of building" to which the Group VI repetition percentages are then applied. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: An architect's design for a barangay health center is re-used, without any change to the drawings or specifications, to build six (6) identical health centers on six different sites. What percentage of the applicable RPF should be charged for the sixth (6th) building?
o: 30%, the same rate applying to the 4th building and every one after it
The 6th building may no longer be charged since only four repetitions are recognized
20%, since the rate keeps decreasing for each additional building
40%, the same rate as the 3rd building
n: The Group VI schedule caps the discount at the fourth building and beyond: the 4th and every succeeding building (5th, 6th, ...) is charged 30% of the RPF for that building type — it does not keep declining further. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Under the Group VI repetition schedule, what percentage of the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for that building type is charged for the first (1st) building?
n: The first building is charged the full 100% of the RPF applicable to that building type. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Both Group VI (Repetitive Construction) and Group VII (Housing Projects) deal with re-using one set of plans/design across several buildings or units. What fundamentally distinguishes the two?
o: Group VII covers several residential units built with one set of plans, typically priced by number of units on a sliding scale, while Group VI covers non-housing buildings priced with a flat 100%/50%/40%/30% schedule per repeated building
There is no real distinction; both groups use the identical fee schedule
Group VI is only used when the PCC exceeds P50 million, while Group VII has no PCC threshold
Group VI applies only to government projects, while Group VII applies only to private projects
n: Group VI ("Repetitive Construction, Except Housing") governs repeated, similar, non-housing buildings under a flat 100%/50%/40%/30% multiplier on the building type's RPF, whereas Group VII (Housing Projects) governs several residential units on one site sharing one set of plans, priced on its own unit-count-based sliding scale. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: What is the base Recommended Professional Fee (before any repetition discount) for one warehouse in this scenario?
n: Base RPF = 5% x P8,000,000.00 (Group I DAEDS rate for the applicable PCC bracket) = P400,000.00. This is the "RPF for type of building" the Group VI percentages are applied to. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)
scenario: Scenario: An architect designed a prototype warehouse for Group I (Simplest Type). The client had the architect re-use the exact same plans/design and related Contract Documents, unamended, to build three (3) identical warehouses on three separate lots. Each warehouse has a PCC of P8,000,000, and the architect is engaged for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS), billed at 5% of PCC (the Group I DAEDS rate for a PCC of P50.0 million and less).

q: What is the combined (cumulative) Professional Fee for the first two Mausoleum buildings?
n: First building (P2,400,000.00) + second building (P1,200,000.00) = P3,600,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: For a set of three identical daycare centers, the architect re-used the same base plans but revised the floor plan and specifications of the third building to fit a narrower lot. Which statement is correct regarding the Group VI repetition discount for that third building?
o: It qualifies for the 30% rate reserved for the fourth and succeeding buildings
It automatically qualifies for a higher fee under Group IX (Alterations) instead
It no longer qualifies for the Group VI repetitive-construction discount, because the drawings and specifications were amended for that building
It still qualifies for the 40% Group VI rate because it is still the third building in the series
n: Group VI treatment requires that the plan/design and Contract Documents be re-used "without amending the drawings and specifications." Once a building's drawings/specifications are revised, that building is no longer repetitive construction re-using the identical, unamended set, so the reduced Group VI percentage no longer applies to it. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Under the Group VI repetition schedule, what percentage of the RPF for that building type is charged for the second (2nd) building?
n: The second building is charged 50% of the RPF for that building type. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: In the Group VI fee schedule, the phrase "100% of RPF for type of building" (for the first building) means:
o: 100% of the Project Construction Cost of only the first building, with no percentage applied
100% of a fixed peso amount set by SPP Document 202 regardless of building type
100% of whatever the normal Recommended Professional Fee would be under the building group (e.g., Group I to V, VIII, or IX) that the design actually falls under
100% of the architect's daily professional rate multiplied by project duration
n: Group VI does not set its own base rate — the "RPF for type of building" is first determined under whichever building classification (e.g., Group I-V, VIII, or IX) the design falls under; the 100%/50%/40%/30% figures are then applied as multipliers of that base RPF for each successive building in the repeated series. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: What are the Professional Fees for the second (2nd) and third (3rd) warehouses, respectively?
n: Second building = 50% x P400,000.00 = P200,000.00. Third building = 40% x P400,000.00 = P160,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: SPP Document 202 includes a specific note attached to the Group VI repetition schedule. What does that note state?
o: The Architect must personally supervise construction of every repeated building
Major adjustment due to site condition will affect the Professional Fee
The discount schedule applies only within the same city or municipality
Repetitive construction fees are payable only after the fourth building is completed
n: The Group VI provision carries the note: "Major adjustment due to site condition will affect the Professional Fee" — meaning the scheduled percentages assume comparable site conditions, and a site requiring major design adjustment can change the fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Under the Group VI repetition schedule, what percentage of the RPF for that building type is charged for the third (3rd) building?
n: The third building is charged 40% of the RPF for that building type. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Under SPP Document 202, a project qualifies for the Group VI (Repetitive Construction, Except Housing) fee treatment when:
o: The architect designs several different building types for the same client on one site
A housing project uses one set of plans for several residential units on a single site
The plan/design and related Contract Documents are re-used for repetitive construction of similar buildings without amending the drawings and specifications
The same drawings are re-used but revised for each new building to suit its site
n: Group VI applies specifically when the same plan/design and related Contract Documents are re-used, unamended, for the repetitive construction of similar buildings. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: One of the sites in a four-building repetitive series has unusually poor soil bearing capacity, requiring the architect to substantially redesign the foundation and structural detailing for that building only. Under SPP Document 202, how should this be treated?
o: The architect must absorb the extra design work at no additional fee, since it is still the same series
As a major adjustment due to site condition, which will affect the Professional Fee for that building
The whole series must be re-billed at Group IX (Alterations) rates
It has no effect — the 40%/30% figures are fixed regardless of site conditions
n: The Group VI note explicitly recognizes that a major adjustment due to site condition affects the Professional Fee, so a building requiring substantial site-driven redesign is not simply billed at the flat scheduled percentage. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Under the Group VI repetition schedule, what percentage of the RPF for that building type is charged for the fourth (4th) building and every building thereafter?
n: From the fourth building onward, each additional building is charged a flat 30% of the RPF for that building type — the percentage does not keep decreasing after the fourth building. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)

q: Group VI (Repetitive Construction) expressly excludes what kind of project, which is instead covered by its own separate group and fee schedule?
o: Housing projects (several residential units on one site using one set of plans)
n: Group VI's title is "Repetitive Construction, Except Housing" — housing projects using one set of plans for multiple units on a single site are instead priced under the Housing Projects group (Group VII), which has its own unit-count-based RPF schedule. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.6)
